dimensions.assessment: Directly affects surviving members of the U.S. Cadet Nurse Corps who served between 1943 and 1948.
dimensions.evidence: each individual who served as a member of the United States Cadet Nurse Corps during the period beginning on July 1, 1943, and ending on December 31, 1948

dimensions.assessment: Provides honorary veteran status, honorable discharges, and specific burial benefits, though explicitly excludes general VA healthcare and financial benefits.
dimensions.evidence: shall be honored as a veteran but shall not be entitled by reason of such service to any benefit under a law administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs, except as provided

dimensions.assessment: Involves minor federal costs related to issuing discharges, producing service medals, plaques, or grave markers, and providing headstones or burial markers.
dimensions.evidence: eligibility and entitlement to headstones, markers, and other benefits under chapters 23 and 24 of this title

dimensions.assessment: Amends title 38 of the United States Code to create a specific active duty recognition category for a single historical group.
dimensions.evidence: Section 106 of title 38, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new subsection

dimensions.assessment: Provides permanent veteran status and ongoing eligibility for burial and memorial benefits for qualifying individuals.
dimensions.evidence: considered active duty for purposes of eligibility and entitlement to headstones, markers, and other benefits

missing_information: Exact number of living individuals who served in the U.S. Cadet Nurse Corps during the specified timeframe.
Total estimated cost to the Department of Defense and Department of Veterans Affairs.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill grants veteran status and specific burial and memorial benefits to individuals who served in the U.S. Cadet Nurse Corps during WWII, affecting surviving members through honorary recognition and headstone/marker provisions.
